## Your part in each phase

| Phase | What is yours |
|---|---|
| [Phase 1. Engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) | Clarify the question with your commissioner, and score the assurance level with them |
| [Phase 2. Design](../02-design/index.qmd) | Choose the method, plan the assurance the level asks for, and name your critical friend |
| [Phase 3. Analysis](../03-analysis/index.qmd) | Do the work and your own checks, and record assumptions as you meet them |
| [Phase 4. Delivery and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) | Write it up with the caveats attached, and get the approval the level requires |
| [Phase 5. Review](../05-review/index.qmd) | Record the lessons where the next analyst will look for them |

## Four things that are easy to miss

- **Turn a request for an output back into a question.** Challenging a brief is part of the job
  rather than a departure from it.
- **Your own checks come first.** No level replaces them with somebody else's review, and no level
  leaves the work unseen by anybody independent.
- **Name your critical friend before you start**, so they can shape the plan and put their own
  time in the schedule.
- **Log decisions as you make them.** A log written from memory at the end is a much weaker
  document.

## What you record

What the project record holds depends on the level.
[What to record](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd#what-to-record) sets out the nine
sections and which of them your level needs. At Level 1 that is realistically one side of A4. The
templates are in [NHSBSA templates and documents](../09-resources/r2-templates-and-documents.qmd).
